title: Ordered integer shifted-unit comparisons for exact inflation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and $G$ a topological group with original internal modules and actions [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Use the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact trivial inflation $L$ [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants], the native K-flat tensor and coefficient unit identifications [def-sfb-condensed-derived-cup]. Write $I=A[0]$, and define $LI\cong I$ by exact localization of the single-complex comparison, and its shift by the existing termwise signed shift comparison of $L$. In any shifted monoidal category, for a unit identification $e:\mathbf1\cong I$, integers $p,q$, and the first-then-second tensor/shift comparison $s:I[-p]\otimes I[-q]\cong(I\otimes I)[-p-q]$, define $r_{p,q}$ by identifying $-(p+q)=-p+-q$, then shifting inverse unit multiplication, then applying $s^{-1}$. Specialize this to the existing first-then-second signed tensor/shift comparisons of the coefficient and action categories. Define first-variable and second-variable tensor/shift squares separately, using the existing strong monoidal core of $L$, and define its symmetry square using the two native signed braidings. These are explicit maps and equations for every pair of integers, not existence assertions.
